highlights.title: Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha?
highlights.summary: A mysterious new AI model called Ox Alpha has driven certain corners of the internet into a frenzy of speculation.
body: The free model was released on OpenRouter on Thursday, where it was described as “a reasoning model designed for coding, sustained agentic work, and production workload.” On X, Stripe CEO Patrick Collison (whose company is acquiring OpenRouter ) described Ox Alpha as “very impressive.”

So who’s actually behind Ox Alpha? The OpenRouter listing described it as a “stealth model” and said it was “developed and operated by a third-party provider who has chosen to remain anonymous during this preview.”

Unsurprisingly, much of the speculation has revolved around China. AI analyst Andrew Curran posted on Friday that the initial speculation focused on the GLM models developed by Chinese company Z.ai, but “this morning people seem less sure of anything.”

Similarly, an article on Wccftech first suggested that the evidence pointed to GLM, but an update suggested that Ox Alpha could be an unreleased version of Microsoft’s MAI. And on Reddit, there’s at least one post declaring that Ox Alpha “can’t be the Chinese,” while another expressed “high confidence” that it is, in fact, Chinese.

The free model was released on OpenRouter on Thursday, where it was described as “a reasoning model designed for coding, sustained agentic work, and production workload.

The destructive powers of a kaiju are measured via an assigned fortitude level. This also determines their class, like the stronger, more dangerous honju and the smaller yoju. Sometimes, kaiju develop fortitude levels that are considered abnormal, which earns them the classification of daikaiju. To even the playing field, members of the Defense Force fortify their powered suits with kaiju remains, which determines their strength, speed, and durability during combat. As these factors also rely on individual skill and experience, powerscaling characters in Kaiju No. 8 might feel subjective or tricky.

highlights.title: John Oliver Embarrasses Trump Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy Over ‘Godawful’ YouTube Reality Show and ‘Real World’ Past
highlights.summary: John Oliver is an outspoken fan of reality TV — but not this former “Real World” star. On Sunday’s “Last Week Tonight,” the political pundit took aim squarely at Sean Duffy, President Trump’s Secretary of Transportation and former congressman and “The Real World: Boston” cast member.
body: “What the fuck are you talking about?” exclaimed Oliver. “First, this was supposed to be a road trip — why are we still in your kitchen? Second, is there anything less relatable than a family whose conflict is, how do I tell my daughter she can’t go to Harvard because we did too good of a job raising her?”

Duffy claimed that the show was shot over seven months and that no taxpayer money was used; rather, the show was funded by the independent company Great American Road Trip Inc., which listed 17 sponsors, Boeing, Toyota, Shell and United Airlines among them, all companies overseen and regulated by Duffy’s Department of Transportation.
“That’s not great! The only worse answer to ‘Who paid for this?’ than ‘The American taxpayer’ is ‘a bunch of companies I oversee and regulate,’” cracked Oliver.
And, when Duffy was pressed about the conflict of interest in Congress, he replied, “Don’t you want to celebrate America?” adding, “It’s our birthday!”

highlights.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
highlights.summary: Linkdaze's smart digital calendar stands out for not putting its features behind a paywall, including an AI meal planner tool.
body: With back-to-school season approaching (or already here in some places), keeping track of everyone’s schedules can get pretty chaotic. Between work, school, appointments, sports, chores, and everything else going on, a regular paper calendar just doesn’t cut it. That’s where Linkdaze’s smart digital calendar comes in — a touchscreen tablet built specifically to organize a household rather than a single person.

One of Linkdaze’s biggest strengths is its calendar compatibility. The system can synchronize calendars from popular services, including Google, iCloud, Outlook, Yahoo, and Cozi, which is a dedicated family-organizing app. This is particularly useful for families where different members use different platforms. Instead of asking everyone to switch to a single calendar app, Linkdaze brings multiple schedules together and uses color coding to make individual family members easy to identify.

highlights.title: Late Clark magic holds off McIlroy and Cantlay in PGA Tour thriller
highlights.summary: Wyndham Clark overcame blowing a five-shot lead to edge out Rory McIlroy with a dramatic three-shot victory at the PGA Tour's BMW Championship.
body: Clark saw his big overnight lead disappear during a thrilling Sunday at Bellerive Country Club, where the US Open champion bogeyed three of his first 10 holes to give hope to McIlroy and the chasing pack.

McIlroy found three birdies in a four-hole stretch around the turn to sit level with Clark heading into the closing stretch, only for his playing partner to post a three-birdie finish to cap off a roller-coaster victory in style.

A level-par 70 was enough for Clark to end the week on 17 under and close out a third PGA Tour victory of the season, following on from the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and the US Open, with Patrick Cantlay claiming solo second to progress through to next week's season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy was tied for the lead with three to play but ended four back after a penultimate-hole bogey and Clark's impressive birdie burst, while Gary Woodland, Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup shared fourth place.

highlights.title: Lanterns Showrunner on Episode 2’s Big Ending: ‘When and Where to Use the Ring Is the Whole Ballgame’
highlights.summary: Full spoilers follow for HBO’s Lanterns Episode 2. After last week’s premiere episode of Lanterns – the latest show in James Gunn and Peter Safran’s DC Universe – got some fans fuming and others interested thanks to the radical decision to kill off legendary Green Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler)…
body: At first glance, this show could be confused with being just another detective series set in smalltown USA. But then a scene like the one that ends Episode 2 happens, and there’s no doubt that this is the space cop Green Lantern, a guy who can fly to another planet at the drop of a hat.

“It's like Kyle says in the bar in the pilot, ‘When and where to use the ring is the whole ballgame,’” showrunner Chris Mundy told me when I asked him about the use of the Green Lantern ring on the show. For him and his team, the decision on when to use it, and when not to use it, was not taken lightly.

“That was a character thing for Hal, but it was also sort of us talking to ourselves a little bit,” he continued. “We wanted to earn the times we used it in a big way. We start small and start kind of playful with the $20 bill and all those kinds of things, so that each time we used it, people trusted us, like, ‘Oh, they're not just plastering everything with it all the time.’ It's those characters [deciding when to use it], and then because of that, those writers who are making those characters do that thing, they know when to employ it and when not to.”

highlights.title: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
highlights.summary: Flock Safety faces a growing public outcry over concerns that its surveillance technology could be misused.
body: The country needs to find a “compromise” between privacy and safety, according to Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley.

“When people talk about just one of these, privacy or safety, they’re prioritizing the wrong thing, and what we have to prioritize as a country is compromise,” Langley said during a recent interview with Fox News. “How do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?”

Langley’s Fox News appearance was just the latest interview he’s given as the company faces a growing public outcry around concerns that Flock’s surveillance cameras, drones, and license plate recognition technology could be misused.

These concerns aren’t just hypothetical. The Washington Post recently identified 46 cases where police officers have been accused of using Flock technology for unauthorized purposes, including to stalk their wives, girlfriends, or exes.

highlights.title: HBO Officially Changes a Fundamental Rule of DC Superhero Canon
highlights.summary: In 2014’s Justice League: War, heroes including Superman, Wonder Woman, and the Flash unite to defend Earth from an invasion led by Darkseid. Batman and Green Lantern are among the first to stumble into an uneasy partnership.
body: Adapted from Geoff Johns and Jim Lee’s 2011 Justice League #1, the scene is a funny distillation of both characters. Hal is powerful and cocky. Batman is observant enough to identify and steal the source of that power within minutes. It also dramatizes one of the Green Lantern mythology’s basic rules: The ring transforms willpower into physical hard-light constructs, but a Lantern has to be wearing the ring to wield that power.
HBO’s Lanterns just pushed that rule to its apparent limit — and potentially set John Stewart up to become the most powerful Green Lantern in the DC Universe.

In Lanterns episode 2, John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) maintains an intricate, autonomous construct while separated from the ring and after repeatedly losing consciousness. The Green Lantern comics contain a handful of comparable feats, but they usually involve veteran Lanterns, unusual rings, or cosmic transformations. John accomplishes it after just two months of training, which already makes him seem like a prodigy among the Corps.

highlights.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
highlights.summary: Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the development of the same AI tools that threaten to undermine their livelihoods. That seems illegal, right?
body: “I think one of the issues with this entire area of law and this entire area of technology is there’s a lot going on,” Cathy Gellis, an attorney with expertise in intellectual property, copyright, and technology, told TechCrunch. “It’s very complex and there are a lot of raw feelings about what is happening, both for and against.”

Last year, in one of the first rulings of its kind, Judge William Alsup ordered Anthropic to pay a mammoth $1.5 billion copyright settlement to a group of writers whose works were used to train the company’s AI models. At face value, this seemed like a moral victory favoring authors, but Judge Alsup actually ruled that Anthropic’s AI training was lawful. What Alsup penalized Anthropic for was pirating these books from illegal online shadow libraries.

“Like any reader aspiring to be a writer, Anthropic’s LLMs trained upon works not to race ahead and replicate or supplant them — but to turn a hard corner and create something different,” the judge wrote, comparing the way an LLM ingests trillions of words to a writer’s study of literature.

highlights.title: Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game after confrontation with Natasha Cloud
highlights.summary: Former NBA center criticized WNBA’s transgender policy. Cloud yelled and pointed in his direction after scoring. Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday night’s Indiana Fever v Chicago Sky WNBA game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.
body: Freedom was sitting along the baseline. He had on a black shirt that read “WOMAN. Noun. Adult human female.”

The Fever called for a time out after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third quarter. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Kanter’s direction.

Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Kanter, 34, as she approached him. A standing Kanter held his arms out and took one step on the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two.
“There was just a fan incident and the security handled it, and we’re just going to focus on the game,” Chicago forward Azura Stevens said after the Sky’s 113-90 loss.

highlights.title: ‘Lanterns’ Episode 2 Ending Explained: Who Are Sinestro and the Manhunters?
highlights.summary: HBO’s Lanterns is taking a very grounded approach to its portrayal of DC ’s galactic peacekeeper Green Lantern. The TV series is mostly set in the dusty town of Rushville, Nebraska, and it’s more focused on buddy cop dynamics and True Detective -style mystery than superhero action.
body: In episode 2, Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) sends his trainee John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) back to his home in Coast City to recharge his power ring and feed his carnivorous alien plant. John is abducted outside Hal’s home by aliens, part of the same group involved in the mass shooting that brought the Green Lantern to Rushville. Their leader, Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor), says they are looking for a Manhunter, which he describes as “one of the most dangerous beings to ever exist.”

Since the Manhunter has taken human form, Antaan explains he can be killed as a human. Antaan plans to blow up the whole town in 48 hours if John doesn’t find the Manhunter before then. Antaan is disappointed by John’s education as a prospective Green Lantern, pointing out Hal should have told John how impressive it is that he can maintain his bird construct without even wearing the ring. He’s also surprised he doesn’t know who the Manhunters are. “You think the Green Lanterns came first? You really don’t know?” Antaan asks.
points: HBO’s Lanterns is taking a very grounded approach to its portrayal of DC ’s galactic peacekeeper Green Lantern.

highlights.title: Clash Royale research finds 85% of rage quitters enjoy gaming more after returning
highlights.summary: Supercell has revealed that 85.1% of rage quitters say they enjoy gaming more when they come back. That's according to research commissioned by Clash Royale, which surveyed 9,000 gamers across seven markets as the mobile game searches for a player to become its first-ever rage emote.... [ MORE ]
body: The research found that Mexico had the highest share of players who enjoyed the game more after returning from a rage quit, at 90.5%, while Germany recorded the lowest at 74.4%.

Globally, gamers said they rage quit because they want to do well (31.1%), care about the game (22.1%) and want to protect a winning streak (21.9%). Brazil had the highest share of gamers who had rage quit, at 77%, compared with 59% in Mexico.

The research also found that close to four in 10 gamers who rage quit have done so somewhere public. The US was the only market where gamers wanted an audience, with 55.6% of US rage quitters saying they would happily post a clip of the moment.
In the UK, 31.5% of public rage quitters had done so in a pub, while British gamers also led in ranting to a friend at 20.8% and screaming into a pillow at 17.2%.

highlights.title: ‘When I make a sale, I’ll sing a high note’: a day in the life of an opera singing car salesman
highlights.summary: Andrew Hiers is trying to start his own opera company. Until then, he’s serenading the parking lot. Andrew Hiers, 38, is an opera singer – a bass-baritone – and a car salesman in Cocoa, Florida.
body: Today, I woke up a little bit earlier than usual, about 6.30. We have an old man cat; he’s 18 years old, and lately he forgets when feeding time is. At about 4.30, he’ll start yelling.

I also returned an email to a young man finishing up his conducting degree. We’re trying to start our own opera company – I want something that’s going to be self-sustaining and generate revenue, whereas a lot of opera companies are based on donations and grants.

Because it’s a long day, I did bring some frozen stuff I can heat up. The other day, a customer I was taking on a test drive said, “Oh, I’m taking you to lunch with some friends,” which is not typical. One of them had seen my story, and he wanted to take my picture.

When the service people go home, that’s when a lot of my big videos have been shot in the store – I’ll bust out a few high notes. Or when I make a sale, I’ll sing a high note; those [videos] really have been doing well.

highlights.title: The Unlikely Place at the Center of China’s AI Boom
highlights.summary: Cheap energy, abundant land, and proximity to Beijing have turned a city in Inner Mongolia into a crucial hub for data centers.
body: Travel just two hours west of Beijing by train, and you’ll find yourself surrounded by the rolling grasslands and ancient cinder cones of Inner Mongolia. This vast, arid land has long been China’s capital of sheep farming and coal mining, but over the last few years, it has become the hottest place in the country to build an AI data center.

In Ulanqab, a city in Inner Mongolia home to about 1.5 million people, nearly 100 data centers have been opened or begun construction since 2016. Chinese companies have pledged to build projects with a combined estimated capacity of 12.5 gigawatts in the city, and over 70 percent of the total commitments have been announced in just the last year, making it one of the fastest growing compute clusters in Asia, according to a research note published by Goldman Sachs last week. For comparison, OpenAI’s $500 billion Stargate Project is set to reach only 10 gigawatts of total capacity when it’s complete.

highlights.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 2 Review & Recap
highlights.summary: Lanterns continues to impress in its sophomore episode, proving that Kyle Chandler’s Hal and Aaron Pierre’s John are just as entertaining apart as they are together. Read our full review of Episode 2.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 2!

Lanterns got a lot of things right in its pilot episode, but above all, the series benefited from the compelling chemistry between Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart. These two can barely tolerate one another at the best of times, and it makes for a hell of a lot of fun. But what happens when the follow-up episode splits this Dynamic Duo up for the majority of its runtime? As it turns out, these two characters are just as fascinating apart as they are together.

Episode 2 features some terrific Hal/John scenes as bookends, but for the most part, the emphasis is on the two men as solo players. While John carries out a glorified fetch quest for his grouchy mentor, Hal sets about digging deeper into the mysteries of Rushville, Nebraska. Needless to say, both men wind up discovering far more than they bargained for in the end.
points: Lanterns continues to impress in its sophomore episode, proving that Kyle Chandler’s Hal and Aaron Pierre’s John are just as entertaining apart as they are together.

body: For a while, it seemed as if this show might really mark a serious first: Grohl, who tends to pepper his stage banter with the F-word at least once in every sentence — used as an exclamation, adjective, adverb, noun, verb and preposition — seemed to be inspired by the occasion, and by the presence of dozens of the world’s finest musicians in formalwear, to be deliberately abstaining from profanity. But if that was indeed a goal, finally, toward the end, he couldn’t help himself. “Ladies and gentlemen, on an evening like tonight, I don’t really know how to say goodbye, because I wish that we could do this every fucking night for the rest of our lives with all of these amazing people.”

Some artists who do Bowl shows with the LA Phil or its sister symphony, the Hollywood Bowl Orchestra, run through something close to their normal set and require whoever is assigned to do the orchestrations to follow suit. highlights.title: How Sophie McIntosh Wrote ‘Benevolent,’ One of the Most Bracing Plays of the Year
highlights.summary: The playwright speaks to Vogue about drawing inspiration from New York’s old reformatory homes, why she still believes in content warnings, and what it means for a play to be truly “political.”
body: Benevolent, the latest work from playwright Sophie McIntosh ( Macbitches ), tells the story of four young women at Inwood’s Benevolent Home—a reformatory house for fallen and friendless girls—in 1917. Directed by McIntosh’s longtime collaborator Nina Goodheart, the play’s action unfolds in a basement laundry room, where the wards endlessly scrub at the most sickeningly soiled sheets on their washboards, with more laundry coming down the chute, located at center stage, at regular intervals.

The four residents have found themselves in the Benevolent Home for different reasons. There is the spoiled, 17-year-old Abby (Livvy Marcus), the youngest; the far more mature Emma (Mia Fowler), a Black sex worker at a “50-cent joint”; the brash Margaret (Chani Reese), whose whiteness has afforded her work at some of the more lucrative $10 brothels; and Sarah (Rachel Ravel), the most buoyant of the bunch, who has been panhandling on the Coney Island Boardwalk (or “Sodom by the Sea,” as Abby has heard her father refer to it). Over the course of the play, we see the women confront challenging truths about themselves and each other, bridging the gaps in their ages and experience.

highlights.title: After more than 15 years of laptops in the classroom, do Australian schools need a rethink?
highlights.summary: ‘We don’t want distraction, we want concentration’: many teachers and parent groups think its time for a ‘digital detox’ Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: Earlier this month, the federal education minister, Jason Clare, took to Facebook. “When I was a kid there was a computer room at school. Now they are everywhere. From morning till night,” he wrote. “I think there is a good argument our kids need a digital detox.”
Since that post, as the minister told ABC News Breakfast last week, he has been “inundated” with support from parents and teachers.

Clare’s comments followed the Victorian government’s announcement that it will abolish the use of bring your own device (BYOD) programs in primary schools and limit screen use to 90 minutes per day for years 3 to 6 from January next year. High schools have been instructed to enforce screen-free learning blocks for all students. The then premier Jacinta Allen launched the policy in July, saying: “Less time on devices means more time learning.”

Computer use has expanded rapidly in schools in Australia and worldwide. “Computer rooms” like those in Clare’s days have been replaced by a laptop in most high school students’ backpacks, touted more than 15 years ago as the “toolbox of the 21st century” and essential to equipping students with the skills they would need for the future.

highlights.title: Over 1 million people have clicked LinkedIn’s AI slop button
highlights.summary: LinkedIn actually announced a "Seems like AI slop" button on July 30th, and the company says that a lot of people have already used it. According to a Thursday post from chief product officer Hari Srinivasan, "over a million people" have clicked on the button, which is accessible from the three…
body: LinkedIn’s new AI slop button is apparently getting a lot of use.

LinkedIn announced the button a few weeks after AI detector Pangram determined that 41 percent of LinkedIn’s longform posts were flagged as fully AI generated, which 404 Media reported on. Alongside the AI slop button, LinkedIn introduced “new and improved” classifiers to identify posts as AI and removed a feature that would “enhance your post” with AI.

“AI slop is a top priority for all of us,” Srinivasan said at the time, and it sounds as if the platform’s changes may be making a difference. In Thursday’s post, Srinivasan said that users are overall “now experiencing 40% less views on what we classify as AI slop from just a few weeks ago.”
LinkedIn is also adding a new message that will tell users who make a post if “Some members told us this post seems like AI.”

highlights.title: Infantino must remember he is European - Ceferin
highlights.summary: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin says his Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino's attempt to sell off a stake in the World Cup was "worse than the Super League".
body: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin says Gianni Infantino needs to remember he is European after describing his Fifa counterpart's plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup as "worse than the Super League".

Earlier this month the world governing body abandoned Infantino's proposal to create a new company - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) - to manage the commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, with 21% to be sold off to a private investment company.
Uefa led opposition to the plan, with its members voting to boycott World Cups unless it was scrapped.
European football's governing body has since said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while the football associations of all the home nations have withdrawn support for the 56-year-old Swiss.

highlights.title: 7 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics With No Words
highlights.summary: When it comes to comedic outlets — be it a movie, a sitcom, a comedy troupe, or even just a single comedian — it’s rare to be a master of both subtle humor and broad, unsubtle comedy. The Three Stooges, for example, are delightfully unsubtle in their brand of violent physical comedy.
body: There are exceptions, though. The Marx brothers are an example of a comedy troupe that could do both. Groucho Marx could deliver a thoughtful quip that might take a second to decode, while Harpo Marx could do something blatantly silly, like getting caught stealing silverware. On a good episode of the sitcom Frasier, David Hyde Pierce’s portrayal of Niles Crane would feature delightful wordplay in one scene and buffoonish physical comedy in the next.
The Far Side cartoonist Gary Larson is similarly a master of both subtle comedy and humor that was wonderfully uncomplicated.

From 1980 until 1995, his single-panel newspaper comic strip featured Larson’s uniquely subversive and silly brand of humor with new characters and scenarios in every strip. Some were broad sight gags that even a young child could enjoy, whereas others could be incredibly understated, and act a bit like a comedy puzzle, where the reader had to examine them to find the joke. Both ends of Larson’s spectrum were hilarious, and that's what kept the comic strip fresh for 15 years.

highlights.title: The new Halloween video game has been banned in Australia – and not because of the violence
highlights.summary: Academics and a former classification board director say Halloween: The Game’s ban due to ‘incentivised drug use’ highlights an incoherent set of standards. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: Halloween’s Michael Myers is one of film’s most feared boogeymen, responsible for some of the most brutal on-screen deaths in horror cinema. The US video game developer Illfonic looked to reproduce those terrors in its upcoming title Halloween: The Game, with gruesome killings a major focus of the gameplay: for instance, you can stomp another player’s head through a toilet seat, or fry their brain by throwing them through a television screen.

But Australians will not be able to play Halloween, because it has been refused classification by the Australian Classification Board, which means it is banned from sale within the country. And it’s not because of the violence or murders.

In the game, players can smoke marijuana to see the location of Michael Myers in order to avoid being killed – a use of drugs that the Classification Board has deemed a “gameplay advantage”. Under the Guidelines for the Classification of Computer Games 2023, video games are refused classification if they contain “illicit or proscribed drug use related to incentives or rewards”.
